events.summary: PKD declines John Brunner's invitation to a UK trip due to recurring respiratory flu (which became pneumonia in 1972/73).
events.evidence_quote: a respiratory flu, which when I had it in 1972/3 became pneumonia, prevents me from making my intended trip to the U.K. I have written Peter Nicholls and told him regretfully.

events.summary: Brunner sends PKD a London Times clipping about William Colby investigating CIA break-ins of left-wing/anti-war activists 1970-72; PKD says it matches the M.O. of his own November 1971 break-in.
events.evidence_quote: I have always believed that it was the CIA which hit my house, and in 1972 asked the FBI to look into that hit, to see if my civil rights had been violated. They told me never to contact them again about it

events.summary: PKD describes Rolling Stone magazine sending a reporter to stay with him for three days in November 1974 to investigate the 1971 break-in.
events.evidence_quote: Rolling Stone sent a reporter out to stay with me three days, back in November; he was mainly interested in the hit on my house

events.summary: PKD praises Claudia Bush's PhD-thesis introduction on his work, especially her interpretation of Stanislaw Lem's article on UBIK.
events.evidence_quote: your paper is very, very good. At one point, the part about Lem, I freaked out... You cut right to the heart of it and made it comprehensible to me.

events.summary: PKD discusses the CIA break-in conspiracy theory with Bush, citing Brunner's London Times clipping; describes break-in M.O. as identical to his own November 1971 incident.
events.evidence_quote: M.O. described is exactly what hit my house back in November 1971... Financial records taken, correspondence, etc. No arrests ever made... the fucking CIA, evidently, all over the US.

events.summary: Tessa buys a horse; the family car needs $300 of repairs the next day.
events.evidence_quote: Tessa bought a lovely new horse. Then the car needed over $300 worth of repairs, the next day.

events.summary: PKD writes to FBI agent William A. Sullivan about Stanislaw Lem and Marxist scholarly interest in UBIK; suggests Lem may be acting in bad faith over a proposed Polish trip; this is the canonical 'FBI letter' on the Lem-as-front conspiracy theory.
events.evidence_quote: Lem proposed to me in letters and through neutral intermediaries, to pay my airfare to Poland... The matter ended when I accused Lem of bad faith, since I later learned that my Polish royalties could be transferred here, and he was not being honest with me

events.summary: PKD speculates that Marxist scholars are interested in UBIK because the novel may accidentally encode a fundamental scientific principle they recognized.
events.evidence_quote: there is a possibility that some fundamental scientific discovery is accidently incorporated into UBIK, by me, and the Marxist analysts in France and Poland... saw this in the novel

events.summary: PKD sends Paul Williams chapter one of CONFESSIONS OF A CRAP ARTIST for inclusion in a forthcoming printing.
events.evidence_quote: Here enclosed is chapter one of CONFESSIONS, I hope complete, plus your letter with my dedication in it

events.summary: PKD develops a tachyon-and-time-field theory for the 2-3-74 visions, drawing on a Soviet astrophysicist's claim that time is a field propagating at infinite velocity.
events.evidence_quote: if time is viewed as a field (as one Soviet astro-physicist does), and it drives forward, then if it has begun to weaken due to the expansion of the universe... retrograde forces such as tachyons et al would be bleeding back at us from the future.

events.summary: PKD encloses a theological reflection on Christ's leaving and the Holy Spirit, arguing the avatar/enlightenment experience became universally available after Christ — and connecting this to his own 2-3-74 experience.
events.evidence_quote: That's why at first when this happened to me I thought I must be an avatar. That's the whole point: it happened to me and I am not. This makes the avatar experience—direct relationship with God—available to everyone

events.summary: PKD instructs his attorney to waive custody of his daughter Isa Hackett in favor of Ann (his ex-wife Nancy's sister), who has been raising her since 1971.
events.evidence_quote: I have instructed my attorney to tell Probation that I will waive custody of my daughter in favor of my ex-wife's sister... I haven't seen either Isa or Ann since 1971.

events.summary: PKD is diagnosed with malignant hypertension; previous medications failed and he is now on experimental treatment, with the Britannica describing only 11 US patients responding favorably to such drugs since 1973.
events.evidence_quote: This kind of blood pressure elevation, which does not respond to medication and which indicates no physical abnormalities which can be treated surgically is called malignant hypertension... I am now on an experimental drug.

events.summary: PKD acknowledges to a fan-correspondent that FLOW MY TEARS was begun in 1970 and rewritten across eleven versions through late 1972, accounting for textual contradictions; praises the Doubleday copyeditors.
events.evidence_quote: I started the novel in 1970, left off until late 72, did eleven versions, and so, doing that many versions over too long a time period, errors crept in.

events.summary: PKD reveals that the character Kathy in FLOW MY TEARS was based on a single real woman he loved, who became psychotic and was repeatedly hospitalized.
events.evidence_quote: 'Kathy' in the novel is based entirely on a single actual girl I knew, and loved, very much. She was psychotic, and I had to put her in a mental hospital finally.

events.summary: PKD writes to Ursula Le Guin thanking her for praise of Mr. Tagomi (Man in the High Castle) in her London speech.
events.evidence_quote: Did I thank you for what you said about Mr. Tagomi in your London speech?

events.summary: PKD proposes to Le Guin that they share a common underlying visionary source — that 'we are twin outcomes of a single underlying experience' — citing Ian Watson's SFS article comparing her LATHE OF HEAVEN to his work.
events.evidence_quote: whatever is influencing my work—I mean, making use of me, really, to put forth this work—that entity or drive is making use of you, too. It is not that I affect you or you me; it is that we are twin outcomes of a single underlying experience.

events.summary: PKD develops the 'we do not dream; we are dreamed' hypothesis — that a non-human artificer constructs reality including 'false work' amid the permanent — drawing on Charles Tart and Robert Ornstein's research on consciousness.
events.evidence_quote: We do not dream; we are dreamed... A prime mover confronts us, and designs the fabric of our night's events... He Who dreams us at night does not also dream us during the day
